segments.text: Euclid's Elements, Book One, Proposition Nine. Bisect a given angle. Given angle B A C, we are to bisect it.

subsegments.text: Euclid's Elements, Book One, Proposition Nine. Bisect a given angle. Given angle B A C, we are to bisect it.

segments.style: speaking briskly, nimble, crisp, and composed
segments.text: Take a point D on segment A B. From segment A C, cut off segment A E equal to segment A D. Construct segment D E between points D and E. On segment D E, construct the equilateral triangle D E F. Next, construct segment A F from vertex A to point F.

subsegments.text: Take a point D on segment A B. From segment A C, cut off segment A E equal to segment A D. Construct segment D E between points D and E. On segment D E, construct the equilateral triangle D E F. Next, construct segment A F from vertex A to point F.

segments.style: speaking briskly, nimble, crisp, and composed
segments.text: In triangles D A F and E A F, side D A equals side E A, segment A F is common, and base D F equals base E F from our equilateral triangle. Since all three pairs of corresponding sides are equal, angle D A F equals angle E A F. Therefore angle B A C has been bisected by segment A F, as was required to do.
